workshops.title: Specialist lab: choose one optional feature and check its policy
workshops.summary: Run synthetic purchase-right, conflict, and lifetime policies. Add one missing conflict rule, then choose one Apple feature with a useful fallback and an honest native evidence plan.

simple.story: A workshop keeps its main job board at the desk. It also offers a courier who takes updates to another room. The courier is an optional convenience, and visitors agree before using it. Today the courier is away. The desk still lets people finish their jobs. It keeps each agreed update under a stable number so the same update is not queued twice by a retry. The missing courier changes the delivery plan; it does not erase the job or make the main board unusable.
simple.meaning: Optional platform features need a policy when they cannot serve the user now. The synthetic watch branch separates feature availability, product consent, and current transport readiness. When transport is not ready, it returns a plan to queue an idempotent command. This helper does not implement native delivery.

example.before: FeatureInputs has available = true, foreground = true, consent = true, and transport_ready = false. The selected branch is watch.
example.change: Call feature_plan with that watch branch and those inputs.
example.after: The result is queue-idempotent-command. The policy calls for a recoverable queued command while the phone workflow stays usable. No WatchConnectivity message was sent or proven to arrive.

words.meaning: A small policy program running on the computer with declared synthetic inputs.
Here, a product right derived from transaction evidence; it is distinct from an app-signing entitlement.
A write allowed only when the stored version still matches the version the edit was based on.
A server version token to preserve and compare under the API's rules, not a number to invent.
A command designed so retrying the same identity and payload does not repeat its effect.
Content past its freshness threshold, which is different from a permanently ended surface.
A usable alternative when the optional feature cannot meet the current need.

simple.remember: Choose the useful feature, preserve the main workflow, and prove native behavior with native evidence.
simple.boundary: The courier story explains fallback and retry identity, not WatchConnectivity guarantees. The helper returns a product plan, not a working adapter. Consent here is synthetic product opt-in; it cannot reveal HealthKit read authorization. Host JSON replay does not establish disk atomicity, cryptographic StoreKit verification, or actual Apple service behavior.

sections.title: Separate host policies, app builds, and service observations
sections.html:
A host model is a small program with synthetic inputs and explicit rules. It lets you check a policy without calling an Apple service. This workshop connects several specialist entry lessons that way. A theme transaction changes a product right, a card edit can conflict, a surface can become stale and end, and a feature policy selects a fallback. The companion has no Apple accounts, signing, network operations, real permissions, purchases, Bluetooth discovery, or health queries. Read the policies end to end, predict their states, and keep those predictions separate from future native observations.

Use Python 3.11 or later with the standard library. Optional Foundation snippet checks require Swift 5.9 or later on macOS 13 or later. No package manager or remote dependency is needed. Run from labs/SpecialistLab: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest -v test_policy, then python3 policy_model.py with the same environment setting. The first command checks adversarial invariants; the second prints a deterministic synthetic demonstration. A demonstration output is not a measurement or the learner's completed submission.

Keep three kinds of evidence distinct. Host behavior establishes only the declared model. Compiling a scratch native target checks syntax, linked frameworks and availability for that destination. Simulator/device/sandbox interaction checks mechanisms that the host cannot access. The supplied NativeChecklist is a pending plan, not a completed test report. You may choose one branch for later authorized work; building every platform is outside this workshop.

sections.title: Check purchase, revocation, and duplicate delivery states
sections.html:
An entitlement here is a product right, not an app-signing capability. Read EntitlementLedger before running it. The fixture takes an explicitly verified input and an owner generation. That generation lets it reject results belonging to an old owner. It stores transactions by identity with a local revision rule, then derives rights from records that are not revoked or expired. The revision integer belongs to this synthetic exercise; StoreKit does not promise that counter. The model does not verify cryptographic evidence, look up products, perform billing, or submit refunds.

Write the expected right for each input: unverified purchase, stale owner, duplicate purchase, a higher-revision revocation of the same transaction, and an older purchase arriving after revocation. The meaningful test permutes the purchase, revocation and duplicate delivery and requires that none of those schedules restore the revoked right. A separate case grants through a newer independent transaction until its expiration boundary. That avoids a mistaken product-wide revoke when only an older transaction changed.

Serialization writes model state into a format that can be read again. This ledger can serialize and reconstruct that state. This tests that the fixture's replay information can be retained; it does not demonstrate a durable disk transaction or recovery after real process termination. In an Apple implementation, StoreKit evidence, customer-facing pending/cancel states, listener lifetime, finish ordering and subscription-specific policy remain native responsibilities. Compare Android billing acknowledgment only at the conceptual level of recoverable delivery and replay.

sections.title: Keep versions, merge candidates, and retry receipts together
sections.html:
A conditional save succeeds only when the stored version still matches the edit's expected version. ConflictStore uses an integer tag to make a stale save easy to see. CloudKit tags are opaque tokens; do not invent integer tags for a real server. merge_fields compares base, local, and server dictionaries with fixed fields. Base is the version both edits started from. Independent changes combine. Different edits to the same field produce a conflict and keep the server value in the tentative result. A real conflict UI must also retain the local candidate so that the user's edit is recoverable.

A lost acknowledgment leaves uncertainty about whether a save happened. This check saves op-1 once, reconstructs the store from a JSON snapshot, and retries the same proposal under the same identity. Duplicate returns without a second tag increment. Reusing op-1 for a different proposal is rejected. A stale tag produces server-record-changed without mutation. Account rotation precedes receipt lookup, so an old completion cannot borrow an earlier acknowledgment in the new account.

A receipt stores an operation's result for later retries. This single-process model updates the effect and receipt together in memory. It does not establish crash atomicity, interprocess exclusion or a CloudKit receipt transaction. Write down the authoritative transaction boundary your chosen implementation would require. For a local document, coordination protects cooperating access but not semantic merge; for structured sync, subscriptions hint that you should fetch and checkpoint changes. Do not treat either a passing field helper or an atomic file replacement as complete offline collaboration.

sections.title: Separate stale content, ended surfaces, and feature fallback
sections.html:
Stale content needs a freshness decision. An ended surface has finished its lifetime. Surface tracks an owner generation, content revision, stale threshold, and end threshold. At stale_at it becomes stale, but a current update with a new threshold can make it fresh again. At ends_at or explicit end, update_surface cannot resurrect it. Checks cover exact equality boundaries, older revisions, and old owners. These times are deterministic product policy values. They are not measurements of ActivityKit callbacks, rendering, or system scheduling.

Feature availability asks whether this feature can be offered. FeatureInputs tracks that separately from foreground opportunity, synthetic product consent, and transport readiness. feature_plan intentionally preserves framework-specific outcomes. An unreachable watch command stays queueable under the product contract; a Bluetooth feature without the required current readiness offers manual fallback; a spatial feature pauses work outside its scene. For health, visible samples can be displayed. Empty or unknown results remain no-visible-data; they do not establish read denial. The consent field does not reveal HealthKit read authorization.

Select exactly one deeper branch and identify what the model omits. Watch needs target/session activation and actual transport recovery. A spatial window needs native controls, accessibility and wearer comfort evidence. Bluetooth needs hardware state and protocol validation. Health needs type-scoped authorization, observed data and background query recovery. Text/media work requires native composition, undo, observation and performance evidence. Shared policy values help plan these integrations, but they are not native adapter implementations.

sections.title: Add a delete-versus-edit rule and plan one native check
sections.html:
A semantic conflict means the intentions clash even if different fields changed. Add a fixed-schema deleted Boolean to the synthetic card. A field-only merger could combine deletion with a concurrent note edit because those changes use different keys. Decide whether your product allows that result. For this extension, preserve both proposals and block publication until the conflict is resolved, or defend another explicit and recoverable policy. Keep the draft and operation receipt. Removing them only to make a check pass would erase the evidence needed to recover the user's intent.

Use a counterexample that a field-only merger mishandles: base is not deleted, local deletes it, and server edits the note. Check repeated conflict delivery, then deliberate resolution and replay after reconstructing the model. Also reject an old owner. You are testing a semantic invariant, not mirroring every internal branch with assertions. Keep the supplied lab examples intact. Make the extension in a scratch copy and explain the changed contract.

Run check_content.py to inspect the assigned JSON banks, allowed HTML, word floors, repository anchors, and registered companion files. It is a local author validation command and does not execute the global builder or record learner state. For any future performance experiment, define the exact interval, correctness oracle, destination and retained artifact before collecting data. Write pending when no observation exists. This evidence discipline is the bridge from senior implementation skill to a staff decision another team can review.

exercise.brief: In a scratch copy, add and defend a delete-versus-edit rule. Run the applicable host checks, then choose one native follow-up and mark every unperformed check pending.
steps: Before running, predict the supplied transaction, conflict, and lifetime results. Record the fixture assumptions.
Add deleted to the fixed fields. When deletion conflicts with a concurrent edit, keep the base, local, and server candidates.
Check the semantic conflict, duplicate input, resolution replay after reconstruction, and an old owner. Keep recoverable drafts.
Run the Python tests, demonstration, and content validator. Optionally compile and run SnippetChecks.swift using a temporary executable.
Choose one NativeChecklist.md follow-up. State the user benefit, alternative, owner, fallback, correctness criteria, and observed or pending evidence.
acceptance: Deletion versus concurrent content edit cannot silently publish a combined result; the policy retains recoverable candidates.
A resolved operation is applied once under one identity and survives model reconstruction without duplicate effect.
Unverified rights, stale owner commits, stale saves and post-end updates remain rejected.
Command output is identified as synthetic host evidence; Apple target, sandbox and device rows remain separate.
The selected native branch has an accountable owner, usable fallback and observable reversal condition.
exercise.solution:
Start with deleted=false in base and server. Let local set deleted=true while server changes note from Blue to Green. A field-only merge returns deletion plus Green without a conflict. That result exposes the missing rule: deleting a card and editing its live content may be incompatible intentions. Wrap the generic merge with a semantic check. If one side newly deletes and the other changes a live content field from base, return a delete-versus-edit conflict containing base, local, and server. Keep that record recoverable. Do not acknowledge synchronized completion while it remains unresolved.

The learner's resolution can restore the card and preserve Green, or confirm deletion while retaining a bounded tombstone according to the declared policy. Use a new resolved proposal and stable operation identity for its retries. Save against the current server tag; if that version changed again, preserve the unresolved/resolved intent and re-evaluate rather than overwriting blindly. Reconstruct the fixture store after the save, then resend the same operation to prove no second effect. Rotation to a new owner must reject the old resolution before checking its receipt.

For a follow-up, choose a watch acknowledgment if wrist access has a concrete user benefit. The native plan separates latest application context from command transfer, defines pending/reply-loss recovery and keeps the phone task usable. Compilation of the target, paired-device transfer and actual background observations are different rows. Another valid choice is a UIKit text command with selection/undo tests, a coordinated document adapter or a bounded ActivityKit view. None is pre-completed by reading this answer.

The submitted evidence ledger contains exact commands and observed results only after execution. It labels JSON reconstruction as model replay, Foundation compilation as host source verification, and native service/device/sandbox work as pending. It states the model's missing cryptographic verification, remote scheduling, durable atomicity and platform authorization. Staff quality comes from a reviewable mechanism and next experiment, not from the number of frameworks listed or a passing synthetic demonstration.

quiz.question: What does reconstructing the JSON ConflictStore establish?
options: The fixture retains operation receipts for model replay; disk/crash/cloud durability remains unproved.
Every native device conflict is resolved.
quiz.explanation: The model can reject a duplicate after reconstruction, but no real storage or Apple service participates in that check.

quiz.question: Why add a semantic delete-versus-edit rule above a field merger?
options: Different fields can still represent incompatible domain intentions.
Deletion always removes the need for receipts.
quiz.explanation: Deletion of the card and editing its content can conflict even when separate keys changed. Preserve proposals and choose a declared resolution.

quiz.question: What is a successful workshop evidence submission?
options: All native rows marked passed after host tests.
Actual host outputs plus explicitly pending native/service/device evidence and a bounded next experiment.
An invented timing improvement based on source inspection.
quiz.explanation: Each evidence class supports different claims. The workbench does not perform permissions, purchases, transport, rendering or performance measurement.
